title: SGB 2021-22 Series I: Up to 167% Gains on Early Redemption
description: Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) 2021-22 Series I has opened its premature redemption window, marking five years since its issuance. Investors opting to exit now can.

faq.q: What is the premature redemption period for SGBs?
faq.a: SGBs have an 8-year maturity period, but investors can opt for premature redemption after the fifth year from the date of issue. This window opens for a specific period announced by the RBI.

faq.q: How is the premature redemption price determined?
faq.a: The RBI determines the premature redemption price based on the simple average of the closing price of 999 purity gold, published by the IBJA Ltd, for the last three business days of the week preceding the date of redemption.

faq.q: Are capital gains from SGBs taxable?
faq.a: Capital gains from SGBs redeemed at maturity (after 8 years) are exempt from tax for individuals. However, capital gains from premature redemption (after 5 years) are treated as Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and taxed at 20% with indexation benefit.

faq.q: Is the interest earned on SGBs taxable?
faq.a: Yes, the 2.50% annual interest paid semi-annually on SGBs is taxable. It is added to your total income and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab rates.

faq.q: How do I apply for premature redemption?
faq.a: Investors holding SGBs in dematerialised form can apply for premature redemption through their respective banks or depository participants. For physical certificate holders, the application is typically made through the receiving office where the bond was initially purchased.
